title: Renewal Decay Mapping — Playbook & Counterfactual Toolkit
content:
Purpose:
A compact, field-ready playbook for diagnosing renewal decay (when a healthy account shows progressive decline) and running short counterfactual experiments to test recovery hypotheses. This is intentionally pragmatic — use as a template during QBR prep, renewal risk calls, and short reactivation sprints.

When to use this doc:
- Accounts showing 2+ weeks of downward signals (usage, logins, embedding volume) after previously stable baseline.
- Renewal window < 90 days and early warning signals present.
- Post-closure retrospective when a renewal unexpectedly failed and you want a reproducible root-cause + experiment log.

Quick start checklist (first 48 hours):
1) Snapshot: get an account snapshot (last 90 days) — usage, API tokens, model variants used, average latency, error rate, support ticket count, SQL billing spikes.
2) Stakeholder sync: schedule 30-min with AEs + CSM + Solutions Eng.
3) Choropleth: flag which product surfaces regressed (chat, batch embeddings, dedicated endpoints).
4) Determine severity tier (see scoring rubric below) and pick playbook lane (low touch, medium touch, high touch).

Stakeholders & roles:
- CSM: lead communications, own timeline, proposal for next touchpoint.
- AE: commercial levers, contract/terms background.
- Solutions Eng: technical RCA, short remediation plan.
- Product Ops / Finance (optional): validate billing anomalies or quota changes.

Primary signals to collect (data sources listed in priority):
1) Usage telemetry (1min/1d aggregates): active users, API calls, tokens per call, batch frequency.
2) Performance metrics: p95 latency, error rates for last 30 days vs prior 90-day baseline.
3) Support volume: tickets opened, severity, response time, outstanding bugs.
4) Cost/billing: sudden drops in posted charges or refunds, quota throttles, overage invoicing.
5) Customer sentiment: NPS/CSAT recent responses, quoted concerns in Slack/email threads.
6) Product changes: model downgrade/upgrade dates, rollout notes that impacted model outputs.

Loss reason taxonomy (categorize into single primary, up to 2 secondary):
- Product Fit: missing features, hallucination rate, or unacceptable latency.
- Cost Economics: per-token cost too high vs alternatives; lack of batching/caching.
- Adoption & Org Changes: team reorganized, key sponsor left, new procurement rules.
- Reliability & SLA: incidents, inconsistent availability, degraded performance.
- Security/Compliance: unmet compliance sandbox needs or KMS/HSM issues.
- Competitive Displacement: competitor feature or price-led switch.
- Procurement/Contract: budget cut, vendor consolidation, legal hold.

Timeline template (fill with concrete timestamps):
- T-90 to T-30: baseline behavior snapshot (metrics).
- T-29: first anomaly detected (who flagged it).
- T-20: CSM outreach and initial triage notes.
- T-15: SE investigation findings and temporary mitigation.
- T-10: Commercial touch (AE negotiation / term changes).
- T-5: Renewal notice sent / renewal position confirmed.
- T0: Renewal decision date and outcome.
- Postmortem window (T0+0 to T0+45): hypotheses tested and experiments executed.

Example timeline log entries (copy into account timeline):
- 2025-10-22: Observed 38% drop in daily active API keys vs 30-day avg. Flagged by telemetry.
- 2025-10-24: CSM (Priya) called user; customer reported increased hallucination on long chat sessions after model bump.
- 2025-10-26: SE reproduced hallucination at sequence length > 2k; mitigation recommended: pin model and enable prefix caching.
- 2025-11-02: AE proposed 3-month pilot discount for Dedicated capacity; legal delayed start.
- 2025-11-10: Customer confirmed decision to not renew; primary reason: procurement freeze.

Counterfactual hypothesis framework (format: hypothesis -> measurement -> short experiment):
- H1: If we reduce hallucination by pinning previous model and enabling stronger output filters, customer will resume daily job runs within 2 weeks. Measurement: number of daily jobs and CSAT on weekly check-in. Experiment: provision pinned endpoint + monitoring + 2-week trial.
- H2: If we implement cost-lowering bundling (batch embedding credits + caching config), procurement will re-evaluate. Measurement: procurement replies / revised PO. Experiment: 30-day cost bundle offer with telemetry-based savings estimate.
- H3: If we shorten SLA response time for P1s to 1 hour for this account, trust will improve and AE will get approval. Measurement: P1 reopen rate and qualitative feedback. Experiment: elevated support SLO for 60 days and weekly summary sent to Exec sponsor.

Reactivate micro-sprint playbook (7–21 days):
Day 0: Align internally, pick single measurable win, craft single-sentence offer for the customer.
Day 1–3: Rapid mitigation (pin model, restore previous config, or deploy hotfix).
Day 4–7: Run lightweight trial with telemetry dashboard shared to customer; daily 15-min standup with AEs/CSM.
Day 8–14: Track KPI (jobs/day, errors, latency). If positive lift >= 25% from trough, move to commercial proposal.
Day 15–21: Close micro-deal or log failure and convert into retrospective.

Sample scripts & templates (short):
- CSM check-in subject: "Quick check: we saw a drop in your jobs — can we sync 15m?"
- Email body (concise): "We noticed X changed and can quickly try a config that historically reduces hallucination and cost. We can stand up a 2-week trial on a pinned endpoint — no long-term commitment. Would you like to try?"

QBR prep & renewal tracker snippet (fields to paste into QBR doc):
- Account health score (numeric 0–100), last 30d usage % vs baseline, top 3 regression signals, primary loss taxonomy label, active mitigation running (Y/N), next step owner, renewal decision date, note summary.

Retrospective output fields (what should come out of the postmortem):
- Findings (3 bullets max), Root cause (single-sentence), Leading indicators (what we should have monitored earlier), Action items (owner | due date | acceptance criteria), Experiment log (what we tried and why it failed or succeeded), Commercial follow-up (AE next step).

Severity scoring rubric (simple):
- Sev 1 (critical): Renewal loss with >$250k ARR or platform outage during renewal window.
- Sev 2 (high): >$75k ARR or major feature/misfit impacting most workloads.
- Sev 3 (medium): < $75k ARR with limited scope regression.
- Sev 4 (low): Small accounts or non-revenue-impact, use lightweight playbook.

Counterfactual scenarios (short examples):
- Scenario A: Procurement freeze -> Offer extended billing terms + conditional pilot -> Measure: signed pilot PO.
- Scenario B: Latency/availability issue after region change -> Route to alternate region + elevated SLA -> Measure: p95 latency returns to baseline; stakeholder confirmation.

Winback outreach template (for AE/CSM):
Subject: "Short trial offer to address [primary issue] — 2-week, no-risk"
Body: "Hi [Name], we ran a focused remediation for the issue you reported (short summary). We can spin up a pinned endpoint with the prior model and share a dashboard so your team can validate results in 2 weeks. No commitment required — if it improves your jobs we can discuss pilot terms. Are you open to a 20-min call this week?"

Data & instrumentation notes (what to collect and where):
- Telemetry export: last 90 days of token usage, per-route error rates, model variant timeline.
- Support transcripts: paste salient quotes with dates.
- Billing snapshots: compare last 2 invoices and credit/refund events.
- Slack/email threads: link to relevant threads and mark key sponsor messages.

Common anti-patterns (what to avoid):
- Trying multiple big changes at once (you can't attribute success).
- Long, vague remediation timelines (>30 days) without interim metrics.
- Over-reliance on anecdote without telemetry.

Postmortem acceptance checklist (finalize before closing):
- All timeline entries timestamped and sourced.
- Root cause identified and mapped to action items.
- 1–3 counterfactual experiments documented with outcomes.
- AE recommended commercial follow-up captured.
- Owner assigned to prevention action with due date.

Notes to self / working hypotheses (example snippets to keep):
- "The model bump on 2025-10-18 correlated with sequence length >2k workstreams failing — could be compilation kernel + kv cache regression."
- "Customer showed adoption drop immediately after pricing change on 2025-09-30 — need billing records to verify throttle or chargeback."

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to attach to this doc when saving:
- Telemetry CSV (90d) link or id.
- Support ticket ids and key Slack thread links.
- Experiment config (pinned model id, caching flags, batch size).
- Commercial offer snapshot (discount terms, pilot length).

This file is intended to be copied into account-level QBR docs and used as the canonical siege-checklist for short reactivation efforts. Keep experiments short, measurable, and owner-driven.

End of playbook.
